curriculum.lesson_evidence: A music showcase gathers your best work: singing, playing or composing. A programme lists the items in order, with the title and the performers. Before each piece, a short introduction tells the audience what to listen for, such as 'This piece uses a crescendo.' Perform with a count-in and finish together. The audience claps at the end. Afterwards, reflect on the elements you used and what you would improve. Always treat every performer with kindness and give feedback as two stars and a wish.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Write a three-item programme for a music showcase and a one-sentence introduction for one item.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: '1. Round (class), 2. Rain composition (me), 3. Body percussion piece (me and a friend). Introduction: This piece uses a crescendo from soft to loud.' The introduction names an element to listen for.

WATCH FOR
Thinking that you must perform everything you know. A showcase shows a few well-prepared pieces and tells the audience what to listen for.

This helps the learner make intentional visual, music, drama or dance choices and name their effect, rather than saying an artwork is simply “nice”. Keep every claim linked to an element or technique.

teaching.model: A music showcase gathers your best work: singing, playing or composing. A programme lists the items in order, with the title and the performers. Before each piece, a short introduction tells the audience what to listen for, such as 'This piece uses a crescendo.' Perform with a count-in and finish together. The audience claps at the end. Afterwards, reflect on the elements you used and what you would improve. Always treat every performer with kindness and give feedback as two stars and a wish. Now choose a different subject or piece to show you can transfer the idea.
teaching.rule: Use the same arts idea in a new artwork, song, drama or dance, not a copy of the example. Review clarity, safety and respectful practice.
teaching.why: This helps the learner make intentional visual, music, drama or dance choices and name their effect, rather than saying an artwork is simply “nice”. Keep every claim linked to an element or technique.
